To smear or rub over with oil or an unctuous substance; also, to spread over, as oil.

examples.text: He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay.
And Fragrant Oils the ſtiffen'd Limbs anoint.

glosses: To apply oil to or to pour oil upon, etc., as a sacred rite, especially for consecration.

examples.text: Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his [Aaron's] head and anoint him.
Anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.

glosses: To choose or nominate somebody for a leading or otherwise important position, especially formally or officially, or as an intended successor.

examples.text: Unlike other previous Prelates, who were swiftly anointed bishops, Francis did not follow suit. Ocáriz remained a Monsignor. In the eyes of many observers, it was a demotion of Opus Dei.

glosses: To mark somebody as an official ruler, especially a king or queen, as a part of a religious ceremony.
To spread (a substance, especially one that colours or is dirty) across a surface by rubbing.

examples.text: The artist smeared paint over the canvas in broad strokes.
In general, all bodies whose surfaces are even will […] stick to each other, and if a liquid be smeared over either surface, their cohesion will be still the stronger.

Then again these figures take no account of the thousands of beggars who travel free in India. Many of these are religious "Sadhus", dressed often in nothing but a loin-cloth, or even less, and their bodies smeared with ashes. A large number of these men are nothing but impostors, but the Hindu railway staff usually are afraid to interfere with them.

glosses: To cover (a surface with a layer of some substance) by rubbing.

examples.text: She smeared her lips with lipstick.

examples.text: A man may bee smeared or grimed, and euerie man shall laugh at him, and yet he himselfe shall not perceiue it a whit.

glosses: (of a substance, etc.) To make a surface dirty by covering it.

examples.text: a pallor which was accentuated by the blood which smeared her lips and cheeks and chin
a rust spot smearing the back of the sink

glosses: To damage someone's reputation by slandering, misrepresenting, or otherwise making false accusations about them, their statements, or their actions.

examples.text: The opposition party attempted to smear the candidate by spreading incorrect and unverifiable rumors about their personal behavior.

glosses: To cause (something) to be messy or not clear by rubbing and spreading it.

examples.text: When she had entered two or three laborious items in the account-book, Jip would walk over the page, wagging his tail, and smear them all out.
Then there are four lines smeared so that I can only read went 5 days ago.

glosses: To become messy or not clear by being spread.

examples.text: The paint is still wet — don't touch it or it will smear.

To stretch out, open out (a material etc.) so that it more fully covers a given area of space.

examples.text: He spread his newspaper on the table.

glosses: To extend (individual rays, limbs etc.); to stretch out in varying or opposing directions. simple past and past participle of spread

examples.text: I spread my arms wide and welcomed him home.

glosses: To disperse, to scatter or distribute over a given area.

examples.text: I spread the rice grains evenly over the floor.

glosses: To proliferate; to become more widely present, to be disseminated.

examples.text: I placed my hands on his cheeks, and this time, I kissed him. “Don't worry, I'm not going to let anything spoil our day. It's just you and me.” A sad smile spread across his face, and I could tell he wanted to believe me, but didn't.

glosses: To disseminate; to cause to proliferate, to make (something) widely known or present.

examples.text: The missionaries quickly spread their new message across the country.

glosses: To take up a larger area or space; to expand, be extended.

examples.text: I dropped my glass; the water spread quickly over the tiled floor.

glosses: To smear, to distribute in a thin layer.
